html:
The Bidhawal, written Bidwell on the map, were an Aboriginal Australian people of far East Gippsland in Victoria, in forested country inland from the coast near the New South Wales border. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Little is recorded of them. Their land was mountain forest and river valleys, and their neighbours were the Gunaikurnai to the west, the Yuin to the northeast and the Ngarigo of the high country to the north. Their rugged country was among the last parts of Victoria taken up by settlers. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
